sentiment.rationale: Siemens raised its full-year EPS pre PPA guidance from €10.40–€11.00 to €10.70–€11.10, a meaningful upward revision, and reported strong Q1 results with comparable order growth of 10% and revenue growth of 8%. The improvement is organic, driven by broad-based growth across industrial businesses, particularly Digital Industries and Smart Infrastructure, with management expressing confidence in the outlook. While currency effects were a headwind, the guidance raise and strong operational performance support a positive sentiment score.

summary.revenue: Revenue rose 4% on a nominal basis to €19.1 billion, and 8% on a comparable basis, with growth in all industrial businesses.
summary.eps: Basic EPS were €2.60 for Q1 FY2026, down 45% from €4.71 in Q1 FY2025, which had benefited from a €2.1 billion gain from the sale of Innomotics. EPS pre PPA were €2.80, down 42% from €4.86.
summary.guidance: For fiscal 2026, Siemens raised its outlook for EPS pre PPA from €10.40–€11.00 to €10.70–€11.10. The company also confirmed expectations for comparable revenue growth of 6%–8% for the Siemens Group, with Digital Industries expecting 5%–10% revenue growth and 15%–19% profit margin, Smart Infrastructure expecting 6%–9% revenue growth and 18%–19% profit margin, and Mobility expecting 8%–10% revenue growth and 8%–10% profit margin.
summary.margin: Profit margin Industrial Business was 15.6% in Q1 FY2026, up from 14.1% in Q1 FY2025. Digital Industries margin was 17.8% (up from 14.5%), Smart Infrastructure margin was 19.0% (up from 16.9%), and Mobility margin was 9.0% (up from 8.4%).
key_risks: Negative currency translation effects burdened nominal growth rates and profit, with Digital Industries most affected.
Macro environment remains challenging, with indicators pointing to muted investment activities.
Siemens Healthineers experienced a decline in diagnostics business due to a structural change in the market environment in China.
Free cash flow decreased due to working capital build-up and a cash outflow related to settlement of nuclear waste disposal obligation.
Integration costs related to Altair and Dotmatics acquisitions impacted Digital Industries' profit margin by 0.7 percentage points.
key_opportunities: Artificial intelligence is a strong growth driver, with scaling industrial AI in core industries.
Data center demand driving strong order growth, particularly in Smart Infrastructure with record-high order intake.
Digital Industries software business showing double-digit ARR growth, with Altair and Dotmatics integrations on track.
Strong order backlog of €120 billion provides revenue visibility.
Accelerated share buyback program creating value for shareholders.

management_tone.label: confident
management_tone.justification: Management language is confident, with CEO Roland Busch stating 'Our strong first-quarter performance shows that we’re delivering on our strategy' and 'After a strong start to the fiscal year, we raise our outlook.'
